title: The house in Johari Bazaar
summary: She grew up above her father's shop in Johari Bazaar, with the sound of bangles being sold below.
quote: We lived above Papa's shop in Johari Bazaar. All day you could hear the bangle-sellers calling, and at night the whole lane smelled of jasmine. I thought every child in the world fell asleep to that sound.

title: School by the lake
summary: Her first school stood near a lake; she and her friend Kamla raced to be first through the gate.
quote: My school was by the water. Kamla and I would run the last stretch to be first through the gate, and the chowkidar would shout at us every single morning. He never once stopped us.

title: Amma's rotis
summary: Her mother made rotis on a clay chulha and always gave the first one to whichever child was crying.
quote: Amma made rotis on the chulha, and the first one, the softest one, always went to whoever was crying. So we all learned to cry at roti time. She knew, of course. She knew everything.

title: Lighting the diyas
summary: On Diwali the children lined the roof edge with a hundred diyas and her father lit them all with one match.
quote: On Diwali we would put a hundred little diyas along the edge of the roof. Papa would light them with one match, going along the row very fast, and we held our breath that it wouldn't go out. It never did. I think he cheated.

title: The monsoon kite
summary: She may have flown a kite from the roof in the first rain, or it may have been her brother; she isn't sure any more.
quote: There was a red kite, I think it was mine. The first rain came and I flew it anyway, in the rain, and Amma was shouting. Or was it my brother who flew it? It was red, that much I know.

title: Maharani College
summary: She was the first girl in her family to go to college, and walked there every day in a white sari.
quote: I was the first girl in our family to go to college. Maharani College, in a white sari, every day, walking. People stared. I walked a little taller for it.

title: Lata on the radio
summary: She learned every Lata Mangeshkar song from the neighbour's radio through the wall.
quote: We had no radio, but the neighbours did, and the wall was thin. Every Lata song I know, I learned through that wall. Lag jaa gale. I still sing it to the roses.

title: My first class
summary: On her first day teaching, forty children and a shaking voice; by the end of the hour they were reciting Kabir with her.
quote: Forty children, and my voice was shaking so much. I wrote one doha of Kabir on the board and we read it together, and by the end of the hour they were shouting it. I knew then. This is what I'm for.

title: The bicycle
summary: She says she cycled to college, though her daughter thinks it was a bus; she laughs that she remembers the wind.
quote: I had a bicycle, a green one. Priya says no, Amma, you took the bus. But I remember the wind in my hair on the road past Albert Hall. Maybe I only wanted a bicycle. It was green anyway.

title: Meeting Ramesh
summary: She first saw Ramesh at a cousin's wedding in Ajmer, laughing at a joke that wasn't funny.
quote: At my cousin's wedding in Ajmer there was this boy laughing at a joke that was not funny at all. Laughing so much. I thought, who is this fool. That fool was Ramesh. I married him the next year.

title: The wedding in Ajmer
summary: They married in May in Ajmer; the heat was terrible and Ramesh fainted during the pheras.
quote: We married in Ajmer in May, and it was so hot the ghee was melting in the dish. Ramesh went white as a sheet in the fourth phera and sat down. Everyone laughed. He said later it was the heat. It was not the heat.

title: Two rooms in Shanti Nagar
summary: Their first home was two rooms with a leaking roof; they put buckets out and called it music.
quote: Two rooms, and the roof leaked in the monsoon. We put buckets out, tin, tin, tin, all night. Ramesh said, listen, we have music. That was his way. Everything was music.

title: Sunday walks to the temple
summary: Every Sunday for fifty years they walked to the temple, and Ramesh bought her one jalebi on the way back.
quote: Every Sunday we walked to the Govind Dev temple, fifty years, rain or sun. On the way back he bought one jalebi, only one, and we shared it. He said two would spoil us.

title: Thirty-one years of chalk
summary: She taught Hindi for thirty-one years at the same school and never once wanted another job.
quote: Thirty-one years at the same school, the same blackboard, chalk on my fingers every evening. People said, don't you want something better? Better than what? Than children?

title: The boy who became a doctor
summary: A boy who failed Hindi twice came back thirty years later as a doctor to say thank you.
quote: There was one boy, Mahesh, who failed Hindi twice. I kept him back after school for a whole year. Thirty years later a doctor walks into my house and says, Madam, do you remember? I remembered. I cried like a fool.

title: Poems by heart
summary: She believes a poem learned by heart is the one thing nobody can take from you.
quote: I made every child learn poems by heart. They hated it. But a poem in your heart is the one thing nobody can take from you. Not a thief, not a bad year, not even old age. Ask me any Kabir. Go on.

title: The last day
summary: On her last day the whole school lined the path and she couldn't say a word.
quote: On my last day the children lined the whole path from the gate, all of them, and I could not say one word. Me, who talked for thirty-one years. I just walked, and they clapped, and I walked.

title: Priya came with the rain
summary: Priya was born on the first night of the monsoon, and Ramesh ran to the hospital through flooded streets.
quote: Priya came with the rain, the very first night of the monsoon. Ramesh ran to the hospital through water up to his knees. He arrived soaked and holding a mango. For the baby, he said. For the baby.

title: Sunday rajma
summary: Her rajma: soaked overnight, a whole onion browned slowly, and patience, which is the real ingredient.
quote: Soak the rajma the whole night, no shortcuts. One whole onion, cut fine, browned slowly, slowly, until you want to give up. Then tomatoes, then the beans, then you wait. The real ingredient is patience. And a little ghee at the end, don't tell the doctor.

title: Arjun's cricket bat
summary: She saved for three months to buy Arjun a proper bat, and he broke a window with it the first afternoon.
quote: I saved three months for a proper bat for Arjun. Real willow. The first afternoon he hit a six straight through Sharma-ji's window. Sharma-ji came shouting. I said, did you see that shot though? Did you see it?

title: Poems at bedtime
summary: Every night she taught her children a line of a poem instead of a story.
quote: Other mothers told stories at night. I gave them one line of a poem each night, and the next night they had to say it back before they got the next line. Priya still knows all of Madhushala. Arjun pretends he doesn't.

title: The rose garden
summary: After retiring she planted roses; the first year they all died and she planted them again.
quote: The first year every rose died. Every one. The gardener said, Madam, this soil is no good. I said, the soil doesn't know that yet. The second year they came. Now people stop at the gate.

title: Rohan's first match
summary: She went to Rohan's first proper cricket match and shouted so much the other grandmothers moved away.
quote: Rohan's first real match, I went, and I shouted so much the other grandmothers moved to another bench. He got out for four. I told him it was the best four I'd ever seen. It was.

title: Varanasi at dawn
summary: She and Ramesh saw the Ganga at dawn from a boat and didn't speak for an hour.
quote: We took a boat on the Ganga at dawn, Ramesh and I. The sun came up over the water and neither of us spoke for an hour. Not one word. That was the whole trip. That was enough.

title: The last Sunday
summary: On what she believes was their last walk, Ramesh bought two jalebis for the first time; she isn't certain which Sunday it was.
quote: The last Sunday, he bought two jalebis. In fifty years, only one, and that day two. I asked him why. He said, let's be spoiled once. I think it was the last Sunday. Maybe the one before. He bought two.

title: By the river
summary: She wants no fuss: a simple ceremony, her ashes in the Ganga at Varanasi where she sat with Ramesh, and Lata sung instead of speeches.
quote: No fuss when I go. Simple. Take me to the Ganga at Varanasi, where Ramesh and I sat that morning, and let the water have me. And no speeches. Someone sing Lata. Lag jaa gale. That is all I want.

title: The gold bangles
summary: Her mother's gold bangles are to go to Riya, and the Kabir book with her notes to Rohan.
quote: Amma's gold bangles, the thin ones, are for Riya. Not to sell, to wear. And my Kabir, the old book with all my notes in the margins, that goes to Rohan, even if he never opens it. Especially if he never opens it.

title: For Priya, after
summary: A letter for Priya to hear only after her mother is gone.
quote: Priya, if you are hearing this then I've gone, and you're being brave, and you can stop now. You were the rain that came first. Everything after you was easier. Don't become a nurse to the whole world now that I'm gone. Sit down. Eat something. Lag jaa gale.

title: For Riya, on her wedding day
summary: A letter sealed until Riya's wedding day.
quote: Riya, it's your wedding day, and I may not be there, so listen. Marry someone who laughs at bad jokes. Share the jalebi. When the roof leaks, call it music. And wear the thin bangles. Your great-grandmother wore them to her wedding too, in a village you'll never see. Now go. Be happy. I'm clapping.

title: Just between us
summary: Something she asked Remi to keep to itself.
quote: This one is just for you, Remi, don't tell them. Some days I'm frightened. Not of going. Of being a bother before I go. There. I've said it. Now let's talk about something else.
